newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian banker predicts leu plunge, C.Bank denies.
newsitem.headline: Romanian banker predicts leu plunge, C.Bank denies.

text.p: A senior Romanian banker on Wednesday said the leu currency was being held artificially too high and forecast a steep plunge after elections, but the government and central bank dismissed the notion out of hand.
Foreign exchange traders said the leu was bound to fall after the November 3 presidential and parliamentary polls, but did not expect the slide to be a sharp one.

With President Ion Iliescu just ahead of two main opponents in most opinion polls, the leu has become an election issue, with economists accusing the government of propping it until after the votes are counted. Iliescu's Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) lies second in the parliamentary campaign.

Alexandru Ghiba, First Vice-President of Bancorex told the newspaper Adevarul that the leu was vastly overvalued at its current rate of 3,295 to the dollar. He said its true value was closer to 5,500 to 6,000 and predicted a slide to between 10,000 and 12,000 within a year.
"The explosion will happen soon," Ghiba said. "Probably in a few weeks, almost certainly after elections."
A central bank statement on Wednesday said Ghiba's forecast was a "false prophecy. It will not come true".
"There is no real basis for any of this," Finance Minister Florin Georgescu told reporters. "Such a rate is unrealistic."
In London, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu told Reuters the currency should ease downwards to 3,400-3,500, without elaborating.
Traders suggested Ghiba had adopted too pessimistic a line but agreed the leu's real range was up to 4,500.
"This is exaggerated. It is an attempt to spread panic and make voters fearful of change," said Varujan Vosganian, an economist with the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc.
"But the leu is overvalued now on grounds of political strategy to make imports cheaper."
On Wednesday, the leu traded at 3,295/3,305 to the dollar on the interbank market and at 3,570 in exchange booths. Cross trading other currencies also fetches more than 3,500.

Ghiba's state-run Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA, posted the leu at 3,295/3,305. Bancorex is one of four banks allowed to set currency quotes to be observed by other market players. It handles almost half Romania's foreign trade.
Recent confusing shifts in exchange controls have damaged Romania's image abroad while traditional hoarding of dollars is expecting to put pressure on the leu this winter.
Analysts say the root of Romania's currency problems lies in a move in March to strip all but four banks of their local dealer licences to try to peg the currency at a high level.
"The fact that we have only four dealers allows the leu's rate to be set administratively," Vosganian said.
Western investors say sluggish reforms have made foreign investment inflows slower than elsewhere in Eastern Europe. Romanian exports have been already hit by the high leu rate.
The International Monetary Fund has suspended loan tranches to Romania to express its disagreement the March move.
The leu has gradually slipped against the dollar from 2,600 in January. Inflation -- at an year-on-year 44.2 percent in August -- will exceed a 20 percent target agreed with the IMF.
Official estimates put 12-month inflation for this year at 30 percent, but central bank chief Isarescu said it would probably hit 35 percent at year-end.
